SMTO-GWT-0064 — SMTO can't change this GPU's power limit

GUID: 082fa65a-d3e1-533a-92c3-beb225606674
Slug: gpu-power-limit-unsupported
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • This graphics card didn't report its full allowed power range (lowest, highest and default), so SMTO won't change its power setting. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to show the power limits for this GPU. If the lowest, highest or default value is missing, or support shows as off, the card doesn't allow power changes this way.
  2. If the values are missing, ask the person who manages the GPU computer to check that the NVIDIA driver is current and supports power-limit changes. SMTO needs the card's full power range and the NVIDIA power-limit option before it will change anything.
  3. Once the power limits show as supported, ask SMTO to set the power limit again. The request was refused before any change, so it's safe to repeat after support is confirmed.

What success looks like

  • The power limits show lowest, highest and default values as supported, and SMTO confirms the new power limit.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't ask SMTO to guess a power value; it only sets values inside a range the card reports.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GPU power-limit configuration was refused because the device did not report complete minimum, maximum and default power limits, the installed nvidia-smi lacks --power-limit, or the provider rejected power control as unsupported.

What this means

  • Power configuration could not establish support plus current minimum, maximum and default limits, or the provider rejected power control as unsupported. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Power configuration could not establish support plus current minimum, maximum and default limits, or the provider rejected power control as unsupported.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect gpu.power_limits for the exact UUID and identify missing limit fields or provider rejection.

How to fix it

  • Run gpu.power_limits for the UUID and confirm minimum_watts, maximum_watts and default_watts are all non-null and supported is true (this also requires --power-limit in the installed nvidia-smi help). If values are missing or support is false, update the NVIDIA driver on the Gateway host; SMTO will not change power without all three current limits.
  • Inspect gpu.power_limits; no mutation is allowed without current minimum, maximum and default.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect gpu.power_limits; no mutation is allowed without current minimum, maximum and default.

How to verify the fix

  • Current complete limits are available and the device supports the intended power operation before mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.
